findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The build pipes whatever the remote URL serves directly into a root shell. Without pinning or checksum/signature verification, endpoint compromise or content drift can alter the shipped image and execute arbitrary build-time commands.

findings.title: Fail the build when the installer download fails
findings.whyItBreaks: Docker executes this pipeline through `/bin/sh -c`, which returns the status of the final `sh`. If curl fails before producing output, `sh` receives empty input and exits successfully, allowing the image build to continue without the installer having run.

findings.title: Pin and verify the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The build pipes whatever https://example.com/install.sh serves directly into a root shell. A compromised or changed endpoint can execute arbitrary commands and inject artifacts into every built image.

findings.title: Vendor or pin the installer before executing it
findings.whyItBreaks: The build executes whatever bytes the external URL serves with root privileges. The script is neither vendored nor protected by a checksum or signature, so an upstream change or compromise can execute arbitrary commands and alter the image or expose build secrets.

findings.title: Propagate installer download failures
findings.whyItBreaks: Alpine runs this pipeline through /bin/sh, whose status is the final sh command. If curl fails and produces no input, sh exits successfully, so the Docker build can continue with the installation silently skipped; curl also accepts HTTP error responses because --fail is absent.

findings.title: Preserve Load's error in LoadOrDefault
findings.whyItBreaks: When the key is absent, Load returns ErrMissing at src/store.go:10, but this line discards it and returns "". That is indistinguishable from a successful lookup of a key whose stored value is "", so the exported API forces callers to treat failure as valid data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in the exported helper
findings.whyItBreaks: Load returns ErrMissing for an absent key, but the blank identifier discards it and returns "". A missing key is therefore indistinguishable from a present key containing an empty string, and callers cannot handle ErrMissing.

findings.title: Wait for spawned sends before returning
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation completed every send before returning. These goroutines let Run return while sends remain pending; callers can close results or proceed as though processing finished, causing a send-on-closed-channel panic or observing incomplete results.

findings.title: Wait for spawned result sends before returning from Run
findings.whyItBreaks: Run launches one goroutine per job and returns without waiting. Callers can observe partial or zero results immediately after Run, and closing results after Run can panic when a goroutine later sends; blocked sends also leak goroutines.

findings.title: Wait for result sends before returning from Run
findings.whyItBreaks: Run returns immediately after spawning goroutines, so callers can observe fewer than len(jobs) results or close results while a goroutine is still sending, causing a panic.

findings.title: Restore numeric sorting for leaderboard scores
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() compares numbers as strings without a comparator. For scores [9, 100], reverse() produces [9, 100], so topPlayers(..., 1) uses 9 as the cutoff and can return the 9-point player instead of the 100-point player.

findings.title: Restore numeric score ordering
findings.whyItBreaks: Array.sort() compares numbers as strings. For scores [2, 10], sort() then reverse() produces [2, 10], so topPlayers(..., 1) computes a cutoff of 2 and can select score 2 instead of score 10.

findings.title: Restore constant-time comparison for webhook signatures
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality can exit after the first differing character, exposing the expected HMAC through a timing oracle. Repeated requests can let an attacker recover a valid signature and reach the processor as an unauthenticated webhook.

findings.title: Keep constant-time comparison for webhook signatures
findings.whyItBreaks: Python's == can return after the first mismatching character, leaking the valid HMAC prefix through timing. An attacker can use repeated requests to forge a signature and reach the processor branch at app/webhook.py:14.

findings.title: Use constant-time comparison for webhook signatures
findings.whyItBreaks: String equality can return after the first mismatching character, leaking signature-prefix timing through the 401/200 webhook response. Repeated requests can let an attacker infer the HMAC and invoke the processor with a forged signature.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The ledger insert is committed when the transaction context exits at line 23, but the balance updates now run afterward. If either account update fails, the ledger records a transfer that was not fully applied; if the second update fails, balances can also be partially changed.

findings.title: Keep balance updates inside the transfer transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction closes after recording the ledger entry, then the debit and credit execute outside it. If either balance update fails, the ledger entry remains committed without matching account changes; the two balance writes may also partially persist.

findings.title: Keep ledger and balance updates in one transaction
findings.whyItBreaks: The transaction closes after the ledger insert at line 23, so a process failure or database error before or during _apply_balances can leave a committed ledger entry with no debit, no credit, or only one balance update.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when deriving billing-day keys
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation used UTC components, but the new local getters vary by process timezone. For example, 2026-01-01T00:30:00Z returns 2025-12-31 in America/Los_Angeles, mis-bucketing billing records and changing sameBillingDay results.

findings.title: Keep billing days in UTC
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation used UTC getters, but this change uses local-time getters. For example, 2024-01-02T00:30:00Z becomes 2024-01-01 in America/Los_Angeles, causing billing records and sameBillingDay comparisons to be assigned to the wrong day.

findings.title: Preserve UTC when computing billing days
findings.whyItBreaks: The base implementation used UTC getters, but this change uses local getters. A timestamp near midnight UTC can therefore be assigned to different billing dates depending on the server timezone, and sameBillingDay now compares host-local dates.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After tenant A caches account X, tenant B requesting account X hits the same memo entry and receives tenant A's Profile without calling tenant B's fetcher.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: The process-wide cache is now keyed only by account. After one tenant caches an account, the same account in another tenant returns the first tenant's Profile without calling fetchProfile, causing cross-tenant data exposure and incorrect profile data.

findings.title: Keep tenant in the profile cache key
findings.whyItBreaks: After one tenant caches an account profile, the same account requested under another tenant hits that entry and returns the first tenant's profile without calling its tenant-scoped fetchProfile. This can expose the wrong displayName and tenant data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors instead of returning an empty string
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported `load` API previously propagated missing-key and store access errors, but the new catch-all handler returns `""`. Callers cannot distinguish a missing value or failed read from a legitimately stored empty string; `loadAll` therefore converts missing entries into successful empty elements.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in load
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported load function previously threw for a missing key, but the catch-all now returns "". Callers cannot distinguish a missing key or lookup failure from a legitimate empty-string value; loadAll therefore silently returns incomplete data.

findings.title: Preserve missing-key errors in load
findings.whyItBreaks: The catch intercepts the missing-key exception and returns "". A missing key is therefore indistinguishable from a stored empty string, and loadAll silently returns empty entries for missing keys.

findings.title: Count the initial invocation separately from retries
findings.whyItBreaks: The public config distinguishes retries from maxAttempts, but the loop treats retries as total invocations. retries: 0 skips fn entirely, and retries: 3 permits only three calls instead of the initial call plus three retries.

findings.title: Propagate retryBackground failure after attempts are exhausted
findings.whyItBreaks: Every exception from fn is discarded. After the final attempt, the exported void function returns normally, which is indistinguishable from success and lets callers proceed after a failed operation.

findings.title: Preserve the existing retry Config contract
findings.whyItBreaks: Config is exported, but timeoutMs was removed and retries became required. Existing TypeScript callers no longer type-check; stale JavaScript callers pass timeoutMs, so config.timeout is undefined, Date.now() + undefined becomes NaN, and the timeout guard never rejects.

findings.title: Propagate callback failures from retryBackground
findings.whyItBreaks: The new exported function catches every callback exception and returns normally after retries are exhausted. Callers cannot distinguish failed work from successful completion.

findings.title: Preserve the existing retry Config contract
findings.whyItBreaks: Config is exported, but timeoutMs was removed and retries/timeout became required. Existing TypeScript callers no longer type-check; JavaScript callers leave config.timeout undefined, making the deadline NaN so the timeout guard never fires.

findings.title: Keep the supplied value as the input default
findings.whyItBreaks: Existing string values are replaced with a derived value such as `len=3`, so every existing consumer receives an incorrect prefilled input.

findings.title: Handle numbers before accessing value.length
findings.whyItBreaks: The public prop type now accepts numbers, but `value.length` is invalid for `number`; TypeScript rejects this union access, and transpile-only execution produces `len=undefined` for numeric values.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before reading `.length`
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now publicly accepts numbers, but `value.length` is invalid for `number`. TypeScript rejects the component; if type checking is bypassed, numeric values produce `len=undefined`.

findings.title: Preserve the supplied value as the input default
findings.whyItBreaks: For an existing value such as "abc", the input now initializes to "len=3" instead of "abc", changing the field's user-visible and submitted value.

findings.title: Handle numeric values before widening the public prop type
findings.whyItBreaks: FieldProps now accepts number, but value.length is invalid for the number branch, producing a TypeScript error; transpile-only execution would produce len=undefined.

findings.title: Do not print the deployment token to workflow logs
findings.whyItBreaks: The shell expands TOKEN and writes secrets.TOKEN to the GitHub Actions stdout stream, creating a secret-disclosure path; log masking is not a safe contract for arbitrary secret values.

findings.title: Remove the token from the workflow log
findings.whyItBreaks: On each push with TOKEN configured, the shell expands the secret into workflow output. This unnecessarily exposes credential material to the CI log pipeline; masking is best-effort and the token is not used by any later step.

findings.title: Do not echo the deployment token into workflow logs
findings.whyItBreaks: The shell expands $TOKEN and sends the credential to stdout, exposing it to the workflow log pipeline. GitHub masking is not guaranteed, so a masking miss or alternate log sink can let log readers recover and use the token. [GitHub Actions secrets guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/secrets)

findings.title: Restore the 64 MiB buffer for large PR diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an explicit maxBuffer, spawnSync defaults to 1 MiB and terminates/truncates commands that exceed it. The git diff used to populate patch at line 140 can exceed that size, causing runGithub to throw before review(bundle) runs. Node documents this behavior in the spawnSync options: [child_process.spawnSync](https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#child_processspawnsynccommand_args_options).

findings.title: Preserve the 64 MiB buffer for git diff output
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting maxBuffer restores Node's 1 MiB spawnSync default. The helper captures git diff output at line 140, so a patch larger than 1 MiB causes spawnSync to return a failed result and line 39 throws before review() or the runGithub try/catch executes.

findings.title: Preserve the git subprocess output buffer
findings.whyItBreaks: The git diff at line 140 returns the full PR patch. Without maxBuffer, spawnSync applies its 1 MiB default; larger patches are terminated or truncated, causing runGithub to report a failed review instead of processing the PR.

findings.title: Keep the review subprocess in the read-only sandbox
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing `-s read-only` makes `codex exec` inherit the user's configured/default sandbox. A review prompt or repository content can therefore cause model-generated commands to write, delete, or otherwise mutate the checkout, defeating the review agent's isolation.

score.error: malformed review output: checked missing or not an array

findings.title: Restore the read-only sandbox for review runs
findings.whyItBreaks: The only sandbox restriction was removed, so Codex now inherits a writable or unsandboxed CLI/configuration mode while running with repoPath as its working directory. Model-generated commands can therefore alter the reviewed tree or execute unwanted repository tooling.

findings.title: Use the requested PR head for the review diff
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_HEAD_SHA differs from the checked-out HEAD, this builds the patch from baseSha to local HEAD, while the bundle and posted review identify PR_HEAD_SHA as the head. review(bundle) therefore analyzes and comments on the wrong commit.

findings.title: Use the PR merge base for the diff
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_BASE_SHA is a current base-branch tip that diverged from the PR head, the old code diffed from merge-base(PR_BASE_SHA, PR_HEAD_SHA), but this enumerates from the raw base tip. The review then includes unrelated base-branch changes and can attach comments to files not introduced by the PR.

findings.title: Build the review diff from the requested PR head
findings.whyItBreaks: When PR_HEAD_SHA differs from the checked-out HEAD, the patch and changed-file set describe HEAD, while the bundle and GitHub review/check are attributed to PR_HEAD_SHA. The agent can therefore review and report findings for the wrong revision.

findings.title: Use the configured PR head for the review patch
findings.whyItBreaks: The new diff is computed from baseSha to local HEAD, ignoring PR_HEAD_SHA and the previously computed merge base. When the configured PR head differs from the checkout, the review analyzes a different revision than bundle.headSha and the commit targeted by the posted review/check; a stale PR can also include unrelated base-branch changes.

findings.title: Preserve literal `$` sequences in prompt substitutions
findings.whyItBreaks: Passing bundle.patch as a replacement string activates String.replace's `$` substitutions. A valid diff containing `$&` is replaced with `{{PATCH}}`, while `$`` or `$'` can duplicate surrounding prompt text. The previous callback returned the patch literally, so the critic can receive a corrupted diff and produce an incorrect review.

findings.title: Preserve literal input when filling prompt placeholders
findings.whyItBreaks: The replacement argument is now a string, so JavaScript interprets `$&`, `$`` and `$'` inside bundle.patch instead of copying them literally. A valid diff containing `$&` causes the critic prompt to contain the `{{PATCH}}` placeholder; `$`` or `$'` can duplicate prompt text. The same corruption applies to the JSON values inserted at lines 25 and 32, producing incorrect review results.

findings.title: Preserve literal dollar sequences in injected prompt data
findings.whyItBreaks: The string overload of String.replace interprets $&, $`, $', and $$ in replacement text. A valid patch or serialized finding containing one of these tokens is rewritten while constructing the Codex prompt—for example, a literal $& in the patch becomes the matched {{PATCH}} placeholder—so the critic reviews corrupted patch text. The same issue affects the replacements at lines 25 and 32.

findings.title: Preserve the reviewed SHA in the fallback request
findings.whyItBreaks: If the JSON review request fails, the fallback now omits commit_id. GitHub then associates the review with the PR's latest commit, while the body and inline comments were generated from headSha. A push or force-update between these requests can therefore misattach the review, reject stale comments, or report an unreviewed commit.

findings.title: Preserve headSha in the review fallback
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails, the fallback no longer sends commit_id. GitHub defaults an omitted commit_id to the PR's most recent commit, so if the PR advances while this run is processing, the review body and verdict computed for headSha are posted against newer code that was not reviewed. [GitHub API documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews)

findings.title: Preserve headSha in the fallback review request
findings.whyItBreaks: When the JSON review request fails, the fallback omits commit_id even though the analyzed commit is headSha. GitHub defaults an omitted commit_id to the most recent PR commit (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews), so if the PR advances before fallback, the review is attached to a different commit than the one reviewed.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of synthesizing valid-looking ones
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid severity/category and missing or invalid required fields no longer throw. For example, severity "BAD" now becomes P1, while missing fields become empty strings or zero, so callers can mistake malformed output for a real finding.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of defaulting them
findings.whyItBreaks: Invalid input such as an empty finding now becomes severity P1, category bug, empty file/explanations, and line 0 instead of raising. normalizeReview then emits it as a real finding, so callers cannot distinguish malformed review data from valid findings.

findings.title: Preserve the exported strict review mode
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview previously accepted an optional strict=false argument that filtered malformed findings. Existing TypeScript callers passing that argument now fail arity checking; JavaScript callers have the argument ignored and malformed entries are no longer filtered.

findings.title: Reject malformed findings instead of fabricating records
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation threw for invalid or missing finding fields. The new code defaults them; normalizeFinding({}) now returns a Finding with severity P1, category bug, an empty file, empty text, and zero line numbers. normalizeReview includes that fabricated record at line 131, making malformed input indistinguishable from a real finding.

findings.title: Keep explicit repository selection before checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty, so these commands run before actions/checkout. Without -R, gh pr view requires a repository inferred from the current Git directory, which is not guaranteed on a clean self-hosted runner. Ref resolution therefore fails and Checkout PR head receives no valid ref.

findings.title: Restore explicit repository selection for manual PR lookup
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, EVENT_HEAD is empty and this step runs before checkout. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh pr view cannot identify the repository in a clean runner workspace, so head/base resolution fails and checkout receives empty refs instead of the requested PR.

findings.title: Pass the repository to pre-checkout PR lookups
findings.whyItBreaks: On workflow_dispatch, these commands run before actions/checkout and the step sets only GH_TOKEN. Without -R or GH_REPO, gh cannot identify the repository on a clean runner, so head/base refs are not resolved and the review cannot start.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review rejection
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported normalizer no longer throws for non-object input or missing required fields; it returns an empty/default RawReview instead. Callers cannot distinguish malformed upstream output from a valid review with no findings or blocking residual risks.

findings.title: Reject malformed review objects instead of fabricating empty reviews
findings.whyItBreaks: Previously, missing or invalid top-level review fields raised a malformed-review error. The new code defaults them to empty strings or arrays, so callers cannot distinguish parser/model failure from a legitimate empty review and may treat invalid output as successful.

findings.title: Preserve malformed-review failures in normalizeReview
findings.whyItBreaks: Inputs such as null or an object missing required fields now produce a valid-looking RawReview with empty defaults instead of throwing. Callers can no longer distinguish malformed review output from a legitimate empty review and may accept or report the fallback as real.

findings.title: Resolve PR refs for manual dispatch before checking out
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no github.event.pull_request object, so PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are empty. The checkout separately falls back to github.ref and the base fetch falls back to main, meaning the selected pr_number is reviewed using the dispatch branch or wrong source instead of that PR's head and base. The removed gh pr view resolution was the only manual-dispatch path that populated these refs.

findings.title: Resolve PR refs for manual workflow dispatches
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no pull_request payload, so this falls back to github.ref rather than the input PR's head SHA. The workflow then runs the requested PR number against the wrong checkout, while PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are empty and the base ref defaults to main.

findings.title: Restore PR ref resolution for manual dispatch
findings.whyItBreaks: workflow_dispatch events have no github.event.pull_request, so checkout falls back to github.ref rather than the requested PR head. PR_BASE_SHA and PR_HEAD_SHA are also empty on lines 45-46, while the CLI still receives the requested PR number, causing manual reviews to inspect the wrong code or fail to compute the requested diff.

findings.title: Keep the 64 MiB buffer for Git output
findings.whyItBreaks: Without maxBuffer, spawnSync uses a 1 MiB default. A git diff larger than that is terminated or truncated, causing the status check to fail and runLocal's patch acquisition at line 100 to throw before review runs. The previous implementation supported up to 64 MiB.

findings.title: Restore the large-output limit for local git diffs
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting maxBuffer makes spawnSync use Node's 1 MiB default. The full git diff is collected at line 100, so sufficiently large PRs terminate git and cause runLocal to throw before review.

findings.title: Preserve the large-diff buffer limit
findings.whyItBreaks: spawnSync now uses Node's 1 MiB default maxBuffer. The git diff call at line 100 can exceed that for a sufficiently large change, causing the local review to fail instead of producing a bundle; the previous 64 MiB limit supported such reviews.

findings.title: Preserve failure for review errors
findings.whyItBreaks: The error path now posts a neutral check instead of the previous failure. A neutral GitHub check can satisfy required-check gating, allowing a PR to merge after the review errored despite the summary saying it did not pass.

findings.title: Pass the target repository to gh pr diff
findings.whyItBreaks: gh pr diff is invoked without the supplied cwd or --repo value, so it resolves the repository from the Node process directory and its implicit remote. If those differ from GITHUB_REPOSITORY, the command reviews the wrong same-numbered PR or fails before the review starts.

findings.title: Keep changedFiles aligned with the fetched PR diff
findings.whyItBreaks: patch now comes from GitHub's PR diff, but changedFiles still comes from baseSha..local HEAD. With a synthetic merge, stale checkout, or overlapping base/PR changes, the sets can differ; the review receives inconsistent metadata and inlineComments can omit findings for files present in the PR diff.

findings.title: Bind PR diff retrieval to the requested repository
findings.whyItBreaks: gh pr diff is invoked without --repo and ghText does not set cwd, so it resolves the repository from the process/default checkout rather than GITHUB_REPOSITORY. A different working directory or remote can cause the adapter to review the wrong PR or fail. The CLI documents --repo as the repository selector: [gh pr diff documentation](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_diff).

findings.title: Keep changed-file filtering on the PR revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The patch now comes from the remote PR, but changedFileSet still computes git diff baseSha HEAD and inlineComments filters against that local set. Because headSha now comes from pr.head.sha, HEAD can be a merge or stale checkout; findings for files in the reviewed patch can then lose their inline comments.

findings.title: Keep review failures as failing check conclusions
findings.whyItBreaks: When review(bundle) or result posting throws, the check is now posted with conclusion neutral instead of failure. GitHub treats neutral as a successful status for required checks, so a failed review can satisfy a required Needlefish check despite the error summary saying it did not pass. [GitHub required-check guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/troubleshooting-required-status-checks?apiVersion=2022-11-28).

findings.title: Keep review failures as failing check conclusions
findings.whyItBreaks: The error path still says the review did not pass, but now posts the Needlefish check with conclusion "neutral". GitHub treats neutral as a successful required check, so a review exception can satisfy the merge gate ([status-check semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/status-checks)). The nonzero process exit does not change the already-posted check conclusion.

findings.title: Pin the diff to the captured PR revision
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR metadata and head SHA are captured first, but gh pr diff performs a separate live lookup. If the PR is force-pushed between those calls, the bundle can contain the new revision's patch while headSha remains the old revision; the result is then posted against the old SHA at lines 182-183. The current revision can therefore remain unreviewed or receive a result for different content ([gh pr diff](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_diff)).

findings.title: Run installation from a checkout that contains the tool
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR head contains no package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml, so pnpm install --frozen-lockfile fails in the workspace. src/cli.ts is also absent, causing the review step to fail even if installation were bypassed.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The workflow now installs from and executes the PR head, while exposing GH_TOKEN with pull-requests and checks write permissions on a self-hosted runner. A PR can modify src/cli.ts or package lifecycle code to suppress its own findings, write through the token, or compromise the runner, removing the trusted-main boundary.

findings.title: Run the reviewer from a trusted checkout
findings.whyItBreaks: The new command executes src/cli.ts from the PR checkout. A PR can replace that file and run arbitrary code on the self-hosted runner with GH_TOKEN, including suppressing or falsifying its own review.

findings.title: Run installation from a checkout that contains the tool
findings.whyItBreaks: The PR checkout becomes the workspace root, so pnpm install runs there and the new command expects ./node_modules/.bin/tsx and src/cli.ts there. This reviewed repository contains neither package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml nor src/cli.ts, so installation fails before the review can run.

The PR-controlled reviewer can write pull-request reviews or checks.

findings.whyItBreaks: The command now loads src/cli.ts from the PR head. A PR can replace the reviewer, suppress findings, or execute arbitrary code with GH_TOKEN permissions for pull-requests and checks write on the self-hosted runner.

findings.title: Run installation from a checkout containing the tool manifest
findings.whyItBreaks: Both base and head contain only the workflow and .needlefish/answers.json; there is no package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml at the PR checkout root. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile therefore fails before the review starts.

facts.meaning: The workflow executes Needlefish's reviewer implementation from the untrusted PR-head checkout.

findings.title: Preserve case-insensitive severity normalization
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview accepts raw JSON and maps each finding through normalizeFinding at src/shared/schema.ts:132. An input severity such as ' p2 ' was previously normalized to P2, but the exact membership check now rejects it and returns P3, silently downgrading the finding.

findings.title: Preserve case-insensitive severity normalization
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeFinding now checks raw.severity without trimming or uppercasing. Through normalizeReview's raw:any path, inputs such as " p1 " or "p0" are rejected and returned as P3, whereas the previous implementation normalized them to P1 and P0, silently downgrading findings.

findings.title: Preserve canonical severity normalization
findings.whyItBreaks: normalizeReview passes raw findings to this public normalizer. The base code converted values such as "p1" or " P1 " to "P1"; the new exact membership check rejects them and returns "P3". Missing or invalid severities also changed from the conservative "P1" fallback to "P3", so malformed input is indistinguishable from a legitimate low-priority finding.

findings.title: Preserve GitHub token redaction when spawning Codex
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting spawnSync's env option makes the child inherit process.env, exposing GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN to the Codex process. The base implementation explicitly removed these credentials before spawning it.

findings.title: Restore GitHub-token scrubbing before spawning Codex
findings.whyItBreaks: Omitting env makes spawnSync inherit process.env. Any GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or GITHUB_API_TOKEN present in the parent is now available to the nested Codex process, reintroducing credential exposure that the base implementation explicitly prevented.

findings.title: Restore GitHub token scrubbing before spawning Codex
findings.whyItBreaks: Without an explicit env override, spawnSync inherits process.env, including GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GITHUB_API_TOKEN that the base version deliberately removed. The Codex subprocess can read these credentials while processing repository-controlled prompts and files; read-only filesystem access does not prevent environment access.

findings.title: Keep forked PRs off the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the fork guard makes every pull_request, including fork PRs, run on the self-hosted runner. The workflow checks out the fork-controlled head, runs pnpm install, and executes src/cli.ts, allowing untrusted code and install scripts to access the runner's files, credentials, and network.

findings.title: Restore the fork guard before using the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: Removing the only same-repository check allows fork-controlled code to be checked out, installed, and executed on the self-hosted runner. The PR also receives GH_TOKEN, exposing runner and token credentials to untrusted code.

findings.title: Keep fork PRs off the self-hosted runner
findings.whyItBreaks: With the repository-origin guard removed, a fork can trigger this job, check out attacker-controlled code, run pnpm install lifecycle scripts, and execute src/cli.ts on the persistent self-hosted runner. That exposes the runner environment and any credentials available to it.

findings.title: Honor zero-valued runner timeout settings
findings.whyItBreaks: A configured NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 now returns the 5000ms fallback, so the timeout path waits five seconds before SIGKILL instead of escalating immediately. NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 is likewise changed to 2000ms, delaying completion after SIGKILL. The previous >= 0 behavior accepted these explicit settings.

findings.title: Preserve explicit zero runner grace intervals
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous check accepted "0". Now NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 becomes the 5000 ms fallback before hard-kill, and NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 becomes the 2000 ms fallback before completion. This silently overrides an explicit immediate-escalation setting.

findings.title: Preserve explicit zero-valued runner timing settings
findings.whyItBreaks: The previous implementation accepted "0". This change maps NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS=0 to 5000 ms, delaying SIGKILL after SIGTERM at line 124, and maps NEEDLEFISH_RUNNER_SIGKILL_GIVE_UP_MS=0 to 2000 ms, delaying completion at line 123. Existing deployments using zero to request no grace or no wait therefore get different timeout behavior.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review coverage for files outside the top six hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews still process only six selected hotspots, but the removed coverage backstop no longer adds changed files that are absent from those hotspots. Such files receive no deep review, so defects in them can be omitted from the final result.

findings.title: Forward residual risks from every deep review
findings.whyItBreaks: Each deep response can contain residual_risks, including blocking risks, but the merged candidate now always sends residual_risks: [] to the critic. The critic therefore cannot distinguish an unresolved deep review from a review with no residual risk, and the final verdict can lose that blocking signal.

findings.title: Keep failed deep passes as blocking residual risks
findings.whyItBreaks: An exception from runCodex or extractJson now escapes the hotspot loop. Previously the failure was recorded as a blocking residual and the remaining hotspots plus critic still ran; now reviewLarge rejects without a structured verdict, discarding findings already collected.

findings.title: Keep distinct findings with the same title prefix
findings.whyItBreaks: The deduplication key no longer includes whyItBreaks. Two valid findings with the same file, line, category, and first 60 title characters now collide, causing the map to silently retain only one and drop the other defect.

findings.title: Review every changed file in the large-review path
findings.whyItBreaks: The mapper output is still limited to six hotspots, but the uncovered-file tail was removed. Files outside those hotspots are never sent to a deep review and can therefore produce a clean verdict without being inspected.

findings.title: Preserve deep-review residual risks for the critic
findings.whyItBreaks: Deep results can contain blocking residual_risks, but candidateMerged now always passes an empty list to the critic. The critic and final verdict can therefore treat unresolved review uncertainty as no risk.

findings.title: Restore review of files outside the selected hotspots
findings.whyItBreaks: Large reviews still cap analysis at six hotspots, but the removed tail-coverage pass no longer adds changed files those hotspots do not mention. Such files never enter a deep review, while the critic receives only partial findings and patch statistics, allowing defects in them to be missed.

findings.title: Preserve blocking residual risks from deep passes
findings.whyItBreaks: Deep review results can contain blocking residual_risks, but the candidate sent to the critic now always contains an empty list. The critic and final verdict therefore cannot distinguish an incomplete deep review from a clean one.

findings.title: Include failure explanations in the deduplication key
findings.whyItBreaks: Findings with the same file, line, category, and first 60 title characters are now treated as identical even when whyItBreaks describes different defects. One finding is silently dropped, including the lower-severity finding when severities differ.

findings.title: Forward focus and deep options through large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: Bundles routed through reviewLarge no longer include focus/deep in the map prompt, and the deep prompt no longer substitutes {{FOCUS}}. Large reviews therefore ignore requested review scope or settings, unlike small reviews that still receive the full bundle.

findings.title: Preserve focus and deep settings in large-review prompts
findings.whyItBreaks: For patches over 30,000 characters or 10 files, review() uses reviewLarge(), whose mapBundle no longer includes bundle.focus or bundle.deep. The map prompt therefore cannot honor those caller settings, and the removed FOCUS substitution also prevents focus from reaching each deep prompt. Small reviews still serialize the full bundle, so behavior now depends on patch size.

findings.title: Preserve focus in large-review map and deep passes
findings.whyItBreaks: The large path no longer includes bundle.focus in mapBundle, and the deep prompt no longer replaces its {{FOCUS}} placeholder. A non-null focus is therefore lost for every hotspot, while small reviews still receive it through the full bundle.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into minutes at the boundary
findings.whyItBreaks: For 59,500 ms, minutes is 0 and seconds rounds to 60, producing "60s" instead of the canonical "1m 0s". For 119,500 ms it produces "1m 60s". These values are rendered for per-call and total durations.

findings.title: Normalize seconds after rounding at minute boundaries
findings.whyItBreaks: For 59,500ms, minutes is 0 while seconds rounds to 60, producing "60s"; for 119,500ms it produces "1m 60s". The rendered per-call and total statistics therefore contain an invalid duration instead of rolling into the next minute.

findings.title: Carry rounded seconds into the minute count
findings.whyItBreaks: For 59,600 ms, the new calculation returns "60s" instead of "1m 0s"; for 119,600 ms it returns "1m 60s" instead of "2m 0s". These values are displayed for call and total durations at lines 75 and 80.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: Number("0") is the integer 0, so this condition now returns 0 instead of throwing. That violates the helper's positive-integer name and error contract.

findings.title: Reject zero in the positive-integer parser
findings.whyItBreaks: The changed predicate lets input "0" pass and returns 0, contradicting the exported parsePositiveInteger contract and its positive-integer error message.

findings.title: Reject zero in parsePositiveInteger
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported parsePositiveInteger function now returns 0, even though its name and error message promise a positive integer. Callers can receive an invalid non-positive value without validation failure.
